story: Tunupa is a mountain personified in Aymara legends as a deity possessing varying attributes. The stories about this deity are often linked to explaining the origin of the great salt flat that surrounds the mountain on its southern side. Partway up the mountain there is a cave containing several mummies, and at the foot of the mountain lies an ancient village.
